In _Johnson_, the court explicitly held that "a defendant must provide specific allegations of counsel's deficient performance to raise an ineffective assistance of counsel claim on direct appeal" (id. at 267). This is in line with the precedent set forth in _People v. Smith_ (742 N.W.2d 321, 326 (2010)), which established that "general allegations of ineffective assistance are insufficient to state a claim" (id. at 328).

Furthermore, the court in _Johnson_ cited _United States v. Davis_ (654 F.3d 761, 766 (8th Cir. 2011)) for the proposition that "a defendant must identify specific errors or omissions by counsel that prejudiced the defense" (984 N.W.2d at 269). This requirement is also reflected in the relevant statute, § 645.01 of the Penal Code, which provides that "a claim of ineffective assistance of counsel must be supported by specific allegations of fact" (§ 645.01(b)).

In light of these authorities, it is clear that the citation 984 N.W.2d 261 provides sufficient support for the claim.
